# How young people in the UK think about politics

::: {.lead}
Between `r years[1]` and `r years[2]`, we surveyed young people across the United Kingdom about politics, from `r age_range[1]`-year-olds who took part with a parent's consent to young adults in their mid twenties. On this site, we describe who took part and what they were asked, and you can look at their answers yourself.
:::
:::

## Four surveys, `r years[1]` to `r years[2]`

Two fieldwork providers carried out the surveys for us. Gallup International interviewed 16 to 26 year olds who are members of its online panels, while Survation reached 12 to 18 year olds through their parents, who first gave consent and then handed over to their child. Each provider ran two waves about a year apart. For the second wave, they first invited the respondents of the first wave to take part again and then completed the sample with new respondents, which is why some young people answered our questions twice.

```{r}
#| label: plot-timeline
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 2.6
#| fig-alt: "Timeline of the four surveys from May 2024 to November 2026. Gallup W1 ran in May and June 2024, Survation W1 from July to September 2025, Gallup W2 mostly in November and December 2025, and Survation W2 from August to November 2026. Each dot shows the number of interviews in a month."
timeline <- respondents |>
  count(dataset, interview_month) |>
  mutate(
    month = ym(interview_month),
    dataset = fct_rev(dataset)
  )

ggplot(timeline, aes(x = month, y = dataset, size = n, colour = dataset)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, colour = brand[["ink"]], stroke = 0.3, fill = NA) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = dataset_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 9, breaks = c(50, 500, 1000), name = "Interviews per month") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = site_caption) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```
